title: Kenyan Coconut Rice Porridge
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN195 is the breakfast-category entry for Kenyan Coconut Rice Porridge. The dessert version with full coconut cream frosting and garnish details is in KEN143. This entry focuses on the breakfast preparation — slightly thinner, less sweet, and seasoned differently for morning serving.

desc: Kenyan Coconut Rice Porridge — rice simmered slowly in coconut milk with cardamom and a touch of sugar into a creamy, fragrant breakfast porridge. The coastal morning comfort — different from the dessert version in its lighter sweetness and breakfast-appropriate consistency.
longDesc: Coconut rice porridge is the coastal breakfast that requires very little but produces something deeply comforting. The rice breaks down in the coconut milk, releasing its starch to create a naturally creamy, fragrant porridge that is substantial enough to sustain a morning of work or study.
ingredients: ¾ cup short-grain or pudding rice
steps: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Drain.
Combine rice, water, and cardamom pods in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice is very soft.
Add coconut milk, sugar, salt, and vanilla.
Continue to simmer for 8—10 minutes, stirring regularly, until the porridge is creamy and thick.
Serve warm — thinner for breakfast than the dessert version.
chefTips: For breakfast, keep slightly looser than the dessert version — add extra water or coconut milk.
Stir regularly — rice porridge sticks to the bottom.
Leftover plain rice can be used — reduce initial cooking time to 5 minutes.
commonMistakes: Not stirring regularly — burns on the bottom.
Making it too thick for breakfast — should be pourable.
cookingScience: Short-grain rice has higher amylopectin content than long-grain — the amylopectin gelatinises readily and creates the thick, creamy texture. The coconut milk fat creates an emulsion with the rice starch, producing the characteristic richness.
sustainabilityTips: Use leftover cooked rice to reduce cooking time and food waste.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Thickens significantly when cold.
reheating: Warm with a splash of coconut milk or water, stirring.
healthBenefits: Provides sustained energy from rice carbohydrates.
Easily digestible — gentle on the stomach.
culturalNote: Coconut rice porridge is the morning comfort of the Swahili coast — the breakfast that smells of home for anyone who grew up by the Indian Ocean.
